verdict: READY TO MERGE - 6 of 6 findings resolved, 0 bubbled
strengths: Follows the sibling spec layout (Intent, Goals, Non-goals, Anti-goals, Approaches, Decided, Builder's calls, Left to the builder).
The approaches table records the rejected options with reasons, and D7 states the identical-replies tradeoff and who chose it.
Fail-open behavior (D10), render-time memory-only reads (D9) and the no-paths-in-rows rule are stated as explicit contracts a builder can test.
The riskiest assumption (drawn text normalizing to the turn answer) is named under 'Left to the builder' as the place approach A can fail silently.
The approach table weighs three matching strategies honestly and drops the ordinal one for a stated, correct reason (the transcript draws only what is in view).
Anti-goals pin the privacy and performance constraints up front: no paths or text in rows, no file I/O in the render hook, nothing reaching the model.
D7's identical-replies rule is careful: it never claims a match it cannot prove and always includes the copy's own entry.
The one place approach A can fail silently (drawn text vs `turn.complete.answer` normalization) is named as an explicit live check for the builder instead of being left to surface later.

important.name: Duration format contradicts its own examples
important.summary:
D6 defines `<dur>` as `Ns` under a minute, but the Goals examples (line 20: `lap 0m 38s`) and the D7 example (line 95: `lap 0m 38s`) draw 38 seconds as `0m 38s`. A builder writing the format tests cannot satisfy both. The examples also disagree with the terminal's `Churned for 14m 30s` style only in that rule.

Also (docs): D1 counts a queued composer prompt as a lap press and D2 classifies a turn as `prompt` only when a press landed after the previous main-loop stop. A prompt typed while turn N runs but delivered as its own turn N+1 has a press time before stop_N, so N+1 is recorded as `wake` (lap from start_at, with `since prompt`), while Goals line 19 reserves `wake` for a turn with no typed prompt. The same press also restarts N's lap if it is delivered into N, and no consumption bookkeeping separates the two cases. The spec does not say which happens or how N+1 is classified.

Also (docs): Goals line 17 says every ended main-conversation turn gets one row and one stamp. D7 (a miss draws nothing), D8 (no TurnDuration line, nothing drawn; two rows within tolerance draw nothing), D10 and the Anti-goals line 37 all allow a turn with a row and no stamp. Intent line 12 repeats the claim.

Also (docs): D1, D2, D7 and D8 cite Builder checks Q1, Q4, Q3 and Q2, but no section defines them and the sibling specs carry no such labels. The reader cannot tell what was checked or where the result lives.
fix: Make the examples match D6 (`lap 38s`) in lines 20 and 95.
Or change D6 to `Mm Ss` from zero seconds up and drop the `Ns` form.

Add a rule to D2 for a press that precedes the previous stop and starts the next turn (for example: a press not yet attached to a stopped turn anchors the turn that starts next), with a small consumed-press marker, and state it in D4.
Or state explicitly that such a turn is a `wake` and why, and drop 'no typed prompt' from the Goals wording.
Reword the goal and intent to 'one row, and a stamp whenever the reply can be matched with certainty'.
Replace each tag with a one-line statement of what was checked, or drop the tags.

important.name: Non-goal swears off TurnDuration durationMs, D8 reads it
important.summary:
Non-goals (line 28) say the mod never reads the TurnDuration line's `durationMs`. D8 (lines 100-103) matches an empty-answer row to that line by exactly that `durationMs` within a 2 s tolerance. A builder holding both sentences has to pick one to break. The intent seems to be 'never displays or computes from it', but the spec states the stricter rule.

Also (roast): D8 matches a TurnDuration line against empty-answer rows only, and gives up only when two empty-answer rows fall in the 2 s window. TurnDuration lines are also drawn for turns that did produce an answer. An answered turn of 14m30s followed by an aborted turn of 14m31s: the answered turn's line matches the aborted row and gets the aborted turn's stamp. That is the 'stamp under the wrong reply' the anti-goal (line 37) forbids, delivered by the one rule meant to avoid guessing.
fix: Reword the Non-goals bullet to: the mod never shows or computes from the TurnDuration line's `durationMs` or `turn.complete`'s `durationMs`; D8 uses the former only as a match key.
Or drop the D8 TurnDuration placement and leave empty-answer turns unstamped (row only).
In D8, compare the line's `durationMs` against every row of the session (answered or not) and draw only when exactly one row falls within tolerance and that row has an empty answer.
Or tighten the key: also require the line to sit directly after a block with no hash match, and state it in D8.

important.name: Queued prompt timing decides turn kind, and the spec never pins it
important.summary: D1 counts a queued composer prompt as a lap press; D2 classifies a turn as `prompt` only when a lap press landed after the previous main-loop stop, and anchors the lap on the newest press at or before the stop. If `prompt.submit` fires when Enter is pressed (not when the queued prompt is delivered), a prompt queued during turn N restarts turn N's lap although turn N never received it, and turn N+1, the turn that prompt actually started, finds no press after turn N's stop and is drawn as a `wake` with a `since prompt` tail. Both stamps would then be wrong, and the JSONL would back them up. The spec covers the delivered-into-the-turn case and leaves the queued-for-next-turn case to luck.
fix: State when `prompt.submit` fires for a queued prompt (Enter or delivery) and add it as a builder check beside Q1/Q4; if it fires at Enter, define a press as belonging to the turn whose `turn.start` follows it unless the host reports it was delivered mid-turn.
Or key the lap on delivery: record the press at the next `turn.start` (or mid-turn delivery event) instead of at `prompt.submit`, and say so in D1/D2.

important.name: state_dir default misstated
important.summary:
D5 says `state_dir` defaults to `.claude/state`, so the JSONL would live at `.claude/state/lap-stamp/laps.jsonl`. plugins/harness/config/defaults.json:12 sets `state_dir` to `.claude/state/harness`, and session-bookmark's notes.ts:12 mirrors that value. The mirror test the spec names would fail against the spec's own default, and the file path the spec states is wrong.

Also (docs): D8 writes rows for an empty `answer`, and D5 stores `answer_hash` and `answer_len` for every row, but D7 never says what an empty-answer row stores or that such rows are skipped when the hook looks up a text block. If they store the hash of the empty string, they join the identical-replies candidate list of any block whose normalized text is empty, or add a spurious candidate.

Also (roast): D5 says `state_dir` defaults to `.claude/state`. `plugins/harness/config/defaults.json:12` and `plugins/session-bookmark/hooks/notes.ts:12` both say `.claude/state/harness`, so the file lands at `.claude/state/harness/lap-stamp/laps.jsonl`. Still ignored here, but the mirror the spec promises would pin a value the spec itself gets wrong.
fix: Change D5 to say `state_dir` defaults to `.claude/state/harness` (file at `<state_dir>/lap-stamp/laps.jsonl`, already git-ignored through `.claude/state/`).
State in D5/D8 that an empty-answer row stores null `answer_hash` and `answer_len` 0, and in D7 that such rows are never hash candidates.
In D5, change the default to `.claude/state/harness` and the path example to `.claude/state/harness/lap-stamp/laps.jsonl`.

minor.name: Anti-goal and Goal contradict D7 and D8
minor.summary: Anti-goals (line 37) say a reply that cannot be matched with certainty gets no stamp; D7 then stamps identical replies with a candidate list, which by its own admission is not a certain match. Goals (line 17) promise every ending turn one stamp; D8 records empty-answer turns with no TurnDuration line and draws nothing. The decisions are the developer's, so the headline sections are the ones out of date.
fix: Reword line 37 to: a stamp never shows a value that is not this reply's own; an uncertain match draws nothing, except D7's candidate list, which always includes the copy's own entry.
Reword line 17 to: every main-conversation turn that ends gets one JSONL row, and one stamp wherever a drawn block or line can be matched (D7, D8).

minor.name: Repo-wide doc updates for a tenth mod are not listed
minor.summary:
CLAUDE.md and README.md count nine TypeScript mods by name. The 'Left to the builder' list names release notes, plugin version and marketplace entry but not the mod list and count in those two files, nor the PROVENANCE or CHANGELOG entries the release rules require.

Also (roast): The spec plans a new mod that mirrors `state_dir` with a `tests/mods/test_lap_stamp_*` pin. CLAUDE.md lists 'nine TypeScript mods' by name and enumerates every mod's `state_dir` mirror and its checking test in the config-key rule. Neither edit is on the builder's list, so the project rules would go stale the day the mod lands.
fix: Add one bullet to 'Left to the builder': update the mod list and count in CLAUDE.md and README.md, the CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry and the docs/RELEASES file.

Add to 'Left to the builder': update CLAUDE.md's mod count and list, add a `lap-stamp` line to the config-key mirror rule naming the mirroring file and its test, and add the mod to README.md's layout.
